text_fidelity_a: GoZafu Outdoor Meditation Cushion Very nice! I’ve been looking for an outdoor-compatible and travel-friendly meditation cushion. This is compact, surprisingly comfortable, and makes it very easy and comfortable to keep your back erect (even easier than my normal buckwheat-hull zafu). I had been looking at it for quite awhile before buying due to its high price, seems like $50-60 would be more in line with my expectations, but it is of high quality, very heavy-duty, and comfortable enough I plan to use it for some at-home sessions as well as parks/hiking/travel (not to mention backyard!). The fold-out skirt is small, but helpful for reducing dirt/gravel annoyances. The design seems like a version 1.5, works well but still a bit rough in spots - at some point they ought to get rid of the not-for-end-user large zipper (or if they keep it, make it usable by the consumer e.g. for laundering the cover). The size and shape of the skirt and seat aren’t 100%, but they are surprisingly good. There are a number of things that could be made a bit lighter, for those planning to go backpacking with it. At some point they may want to consider an “xl” model as well, I am 5’10”, athletic/muscular build, 180#, and though I understand the seat is only intended to support the sit bones, it is very close, and I’m used to having another inch or so of coverage on either side, and the skirt - while helpful - is still small enough that my knees can have ground contact. That said, very well done. Don’t know why noone’s done something like this before.
text_fidelity_b: GoZafu Outdoor Meditation Cushion

text_fidelity_a:
NHL Sting Ray Air Powered Hockey Table - 84 Inch - Features Scratch Resistant Material, Automatic Scoring, and Complete with All Accessories Mostly this is excellent, but it could have been so much more!

Putting this together is easy enough, nicer to have two pairs of hands on the job, no problem with only one. Then you get to use it. Lets start with whats right.
You plug it in, pop up the score board, switch it all on and you are off! The sound effects really help, the fun is fast and furious, the game play is great. It senses goals well, had no false goals or missed ones - just perfect.

What really lets this down is the power. The line to an outlet has a little inline rotating switch (like you get on cheap light fittings) just hanging below the table so you have to scramble on the floor to start and stop the fan.
The gaming computer runs on batteries! The batteries go to a plug on the computer! How stupid is that?
There should be a toggle switch on the underside of the table. That should power the fan, AND a 3.5 v power pack for the computer. For the price, it is insane that it does not have this, and I would see that as a deal breaker. I dont want to have to get on my back, underneath the table, unscrewing the battery case and replacing the batteries once every few months. I am modifying mine to work of one simple switch. That is how it should have shipped.
text_fidelity_b: NHL Sting Ray Air Powered Hockey Table - 84 Inch - Features Scratch Resistant Material, Automatic Scoring, and Complete with All Accessories

I used it two or three times in the intervening months and when I went to move the mount, to make room for some new gear, the mount broke. The plastic cracked along a line where the plastic was bent to make it confirm to the handlebars.

I wrote to Blitzu and received a robotic response that assured me they would be back to me as soon as possible. After a couple of weeks with no contact I wrote again. The second time I did not even get the robotic response.

So I got about 1 hour of use out of the light and now I guess Ill buy another brand and hope for better luck.

UPDATe

I bought Super Bright Bike Light USB Rechargeable, Te-Rich 1200 Lumens Waterproof Road/Mountain Bicycle Headlight and LED Taillight Set with 4400 mAh Battery to replace the BLITZU.

Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.

- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.

text_fidelity_a:
WaterRower Club Rowing Machine w/ S4 Monitor & Hi Rise Attachment A few people have complained about putting the Hi-Rise legs on the WaterRower, and they gave it a low rating for that reason. I’m an old lady and I figured out how to do it. I’m writing this review with a few tips to show that it really is EASY. The WaterRower is a fantastic way to keep old tired muscles in shape, and even people who are not that good at DIY (like me) can put it together themselves.

#1 You need a POWER DRILL for the screws (only for the Hi-Rise screws, not for the rest of the WaterRower). Reason is because the screws are going into hard wood. Same “screw hole,” but these are different screws. An “extender” for the screw bit is useful, but may not be necessary (my screw extender is around 4”). Everybody should have a power drill. Borrow one if you don’t have one.

#2 IMPORTANT: The screws to attach the Hi-Rise are not the same screws as for the rubber pads. They are shorter, have a flat head, and different screw threads. You're supposed to get a bag of 16 DIFFERENT screws for the Hi-Rise. If you try to use the screws from the rubber pads that came on the rails, you will not be able to get them into the hard wood, so don’t even try. I ordered my WaterRower from a third party on Amazon, and it was perfect, except that the bag of screws for the Hi-Rise was not included. If that happens, call WaterRower. They sent me a bag of screws, even extra screws, and I got them in the mail the next day.

#3 Get a DRY bar of soap (or some hard wax, like from a candle). Roll the screws back and forth in the dry soap wax to cover as much of the screw’s thread as possible, including the tip of the screw.

#4 You don’t need to drill a pilot hole for the screws because they already have a pilot hole from the screws for the rubber pads that came on the rails. You don’t need to drill the hole bigger.

#5 Use the power drill to slowly drill the screws in as far as they comfortably go, without any strain, then back them out. Do this a few times, in and out, and they will then go all the way in without effort. If you manhandle the screw, it can strip the screw and then you’d have to use Vice-Grips to get the screw out. If you go in and out, slowly, several times, with the soap wax on the screw, it will go all the way in without effort, without any manhandling.

The rest of the assembly of the WaterRower is a breeze. A few people have complained about putting on the Hi-Rise legs, but it sure does make a difference getting on and off the machine, especially if you are an old lady with arthritis in the knees.

ALSO, if you buy from a third party, know that if you call WaterRower, they will register your machine (get the serial number off the back of the meter on it), and you will get two additional years of Warranty for FREE. I was also told, after registering, that the water purification tablets are free, for the lifetime of the machine. They sent me a few extra tablets with the screws.

AND ALSO - please note: I asked WaterRower if it's a good idea to install the Hi-Rise legs first, before assembling the rest of the machine, and they said yes, it's fine, no problem with assembling the rest if you do the Hi-Rise legs first.

If you live within driving distance they will even assemble your machine for you for free, no matter where you bought it, if you have a vehicle that can transport it back home. They can’t ship a fully assembled WaterRower.

The WaterRower people are friendly, helpful, and very accommodating!
text_fidelity_b: WaterRower Club Rowing Machine w/ S4 Monitor & Hi Rise Attachment

SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

Contigo AUTOSEAL Grace Reusable Water Bottle, 24oz, Citron First off, let me start by saying that I am a loyal Contigo customer. I absolutely LOVE my Contigo Autoseal West Loop Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Easy-Clean Lid, and sing its praises frequently. I purchased the Grace water bottle to throw in my day pack when working at my son's cub scout camp. Here are the reasons I chose it:

1. It's Contigo. I like their beverage containers, and they have wonderful customer service - they stand behind their products.
2. It was $10.40.
3. It's BPA-free plastic, and doesn't feel flimsy. I love my stainless steel mug, but since I'm going to be using this primarily in the woods, I didn't want to risk dropping my steel mug on the ground and breaking it.
2. It's easy to fill with both water and ice. We have water stations set up around camp, and I generally fill the bottle at home in the morning with ice, and refill throughout the day with water.
4. It's a streamlined design, and doesn't take up much room in my pack.
5. It doesn't leak when filled properly (note - you have to be attentive to where you fill the bottle - you don't want to fill it above the shoulder, or the bottle will likely leak).
6. It's easy to use & drink from.
7. It's generally easy to clean and has no funky odors.
8. It fits into my car's cup holders.

Here are things that would make it better:
1. Adding a carabineer to the loop, or having built-in carabineer as part of the loop for clipping onto a day pack or bag, similar to some of Contigo's other Autoseal bottles. I've done this for my bottle, but I had to purchase this separately.
2. Double-wall insulation. The thing I love about my stainless Contigo mug is that it keeps my coffee hot and my iced drinks cold (and my ice cubes from melting) for hours - with no transference of the heat/cold to the outer wall of the mug. The Grace bottle does not keep water cold, and it will "sweat" when it's filled with iced drinks.
3. Having an "easy clean" lid. My stainless travel mug (are you sensing a theme, here?) has a fantastic easy clean lid, with parts that swing out on hinges to get into all the crevices, ensuring a better cleaning.

But this bottle was $10.40, not $25. And for that price and my purposes, it works, and I'm happy with it!

Note - I purchased a Contigo Cortland water bottle with easy-clean lid for my son a few months ago, and it has begun to leak. I called Contigo, and they told me that this is a known issue with the Cortland design - not the design I am reviewing here. After I fill out their form and submit two pictures of the bottle (one of the lid, one of the entire bottle), they will replace it for me, even though I don't have the receipt anymore (it was not purchased through Amazon). Again - Contigo has great customer service!
text_fidelity_b: Contigo AUTOSEAL Grace Reusable Water Bottle, 24oz, Citron

1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage The stand holds the bike upright and so it will not fall sideways.
Because it grips the front wheel so that it cannot turn right or left.

Nor slip backwards out.
And as you can see in the picture the bottom of the stand makes the bile roll back uphill,
and so gravity holds the bike from rolling backwards.

I do not agree with those who say this should work to hold a bike in the back of a pickup.
The bike could bounce out (overcome gravity) and roll backwards out.

In the garage, you will want a cover over the bike and stand to keep dust and dirt
out of the parts that have grease (the chain for instance).

Indoors you need a long pad (like an exercise pad to keep the dirty tires off the carpet.

Another (better for cleanliness) is a 'work stand' because these hold the bike in the air
and only the stand touches the floor (like a Park brand work stand). But these take about
15 seconds to load and unload the bike instead of 2 seconds like this Bikehand parking rack.
And work stands are much more expensive.
But a work stand hold bike so that you can do mechanical work on it, thus saving paying
hundreds to a bike shop for repacking bearings and such that you can do yourself with
a work stand and some specialized bike tools.

There are lots of other ways to go too, holders that mount to the wall or ceiling,
some have hoist ropes to raise and lower.

This stand is a very sensible and cheap solution, just keep in mind when the
bike is in a garage, then it needs a cover (cloth or plastic). Amazon sells
lots of these covers, they cost less than this stand.
text_fidelity_b: 1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage

text_fidelity_a:
Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light I commute by bike and I'm obsessed with seeing and being seen at night. I have a 650 lumen TerraLUX TT-5 flashlight (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009WFA4KU/) strapped to my handlebars as my primary light. I added this helmet-mounted light set as redundancy / extra security. I've had it about a month now.

This is a pretty good light. It's fairly bright, and I like that it has amber LED's on both sides of both the front and rear light. This makes you visible from any angle (hence the "360" in the name). Having gotten used to the blinding, virtual daylight of the 650 lumen flashlight on my handlebars, the 250 lumens that this light puts out on max doesn't seem quite bright enough to me. But I could get home safely with this alone if my flashlight were to fail, so it's bright enough.

Things I like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) You can aim the light wherever you need it. It's handy for checking out turns before you've made the turn. And I can now see the display from my bike computer without having to wait for a streetlight! And when I'm off my bike, I can see my lock, into my trunk bag, etc.
2) They increase visibility and therefore safety.
3) You'll probably leave them mounted to your helmet most of the time, so you're less likely to forget them. And if you're locking your bike up somewhere you'll probably take your helmet with you, so you'll automatically take your lights too - less chance of theft.

Things I like about this light in particular:
1) It's one of the brighter ones available.
2) It actively aims LED's in every direction, making you highly visible.
3) It's rechargeable and charges via USB.

Things I don't like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) They add weight to your head / neck.
2) They can get knocked around. I take my bike on the train for a portion of my commute, and when we near my stop I have my helmet on and am ready to get my bike out of the rack to disembark; meanwhile other riders are trying to get to their bikes. I frequently bang one or the other of the lights on the overhand above the bikes while we're all jostling around. Also, when I take my helmet off I feel I have to be more careful about stowing it so the lights don't get knocked about.

Things I don't like about this light in particular:
1) It's surprisingly heavy, and it's unbalanced. The front light is virtually weightless. The rear light, which has the battery pack, is surprisingly heavy. I invested in a very nice, "barely there" helmet that weighs virtually nothing. This light makes it feel like a brick. Obviously it's not that heavy, but it is heavier than I expected. And I don't like that all the weight is to the rear. This is okay when I'm leaning forward in riding position, but when I'm stopped at a light or otherwise upright, the weight is pulling my head back.
2) I find the rubberized button to turn it on / change modes difficult to feel and manipulate while I'm riding. If I don't take the train home, my commute is an hour and 15 minutes. To save battery I have it on low when I'm riding on well-lit streets and switch to high otherwise. I've had this light almost a month and I'm not getting better at feeling / adjusting the light. It takes concentration away from riding while I fiddle with it.
3) The tail light mode is not adjustable. It does this odd, slow fade-in / fade-out and that's it. You can't make it be always on, and you can't make it actually flash.
4) You can't have just the taillight on. Once the headlight's on, you can turn the taillight off independently, but you can't ride with just the taillight.
5) The battery is not replaceable. My flashlight / headlight runs on a replaceable, rechargeable battery, which means I can keep a spare battery in my pouch and be sure I have enough battery to get home. I can also ride with one battery while the other's at home recharging. With this light, if the battery runs out you can't use the light until you get to a USB charger. And it takes a good few hours to recharge, so you can't go riding for the hours it takes to recharge. And the low battery indicator is tucked away at the bottom of the taillight, and is only visible after you've plugged it in to recharge, so that doesn't help. So you'd better keep it charged.
6) You can change the angle of the front light, but only in discrete clicks. Each click is a very small angle of change on the device, but changes where the light hits the road by about 20'. I frequently want the light right in between two of the clicks and I can't put it there.
7) The helmet mounts strike me as odd. The front light slides into it's mount and clicks in place, but it slides in from the bottom. That means the if the clicky thing ever fails the light will slide out. If it slid in from the top gravity would keep it in place. And the rear light presses on with four tabs clicking into four slots. You really have to pull on it to dismount it. Odd.

Hmmm. Looking at this review there are way more things in the "don't like about this light" section than elsewhere, which makes it seem like I don't like this light. That's not true. None of the "don't likes" are show-stoppers. I'm keeping the light and I do like it. They're mostly just areas where I feel like the light could be somewhat better. If you buy this light you'll definitely be seen, you'll see where you're going, and you'll probably be happy you have it. These are just my observations for whatever they may be worth to you.
text_fidelity_b: Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light

text_fidelity_a: Rapidfire Chimney Starter I'm very upset at the quality of this item I just purchased brand new.  I just used it yesterday for the first time along with my new Weber grill, filled it with plain charcoal only to where the top hole is on the top (we counted 50 briquettes), and THIS is what my brand new charcoal starter now looks like!  SEE THE PICTURES I JUST TOOK, 2 from the outside (left and right sides) and two from the inside (left and right). After the first 10 minutes, I saw that the charcoal on the top was still completely black with no signs of the flame touching them.  Just then, I saw a very strange chemical-type reaction occurring on the outside of the canister!  It was as if a magic invisible paintbrush with white paint on it was stroking heavy stripes of paint around the outside of it!  We were shocked to see this odd thing happening!  About 15 minutes later, We finally saw small flames inside that were approaching the top briquettes.  As soon as we saw the top ones beginning to get a little grey color, we emptied it out, and the whole process took 30 minutes -- not the 15-20 we were expecting.  After we poured in the briquettes, which were already fully completely white and falling apart at the bottom, we began to cook with what remained in the canister.  I don't think this thing was operating properly at all, and I knew something was wrong when I saw this horrible discoloration happening only 10 minutes into the process.  I feel like this was made with some cheap foreign material and am very upset that my new chimney starter was ruined and unable to perform on DAY ONE.  I don't even think this thing is safe, because if it's being compromised in this way and the metal is underperforming, who knows what's going to happen to the metal on SUBSEQUENT uses, the metal and the bolts that is supposedly holding the handle onto the canister??  Is this now going to melt and break off just as we're holding onto it and unloading it into the grill??
text_fidelity_b: Rapidfire Chimney Starter

I weigh 220lbs.

Overall this is a great and sturdy scooter that reduces range anxiety and should be able to get you anywhere within a city.

Note: initially my regen brakes would cut on fully (and seemingly randomly) when I put very light pressure on the brakes. This would happen once for every ~50 times I hit the brakes. This lead to unexpected moments where I would almost get thrown off the scooter. Completely unexpected and super dangerous. I'm very experienced at scootering, skateboarding, biking, and this almost wiped me out each time. This happened for the first week, then suddenly stopped. I had just set the scooter up for return shipping and my last ride (to be completely sure) did not have the problem.

——————-old KS5 review—————-
Update: I’m on my fourth rear fender. They break under normal road vibration. Fracture, crack, break at the base where the fender rises from the deck of the scooter. Four different fenders. No collisions or crashes. This one part needs a redesign.

———————

When the scooter first arrived I was VERY impressed by the build and weight. This thing is a beauty. Ship packaging was adequate with lots of cardboard keeping everything separate and stationary.

Assembly was very simple. Just a few screws to attach and an app to download from the IOS appstore.

Second impression was pretty poor however. Could not get the handlebar post straight - even with max strength. And could not get the headlights to turn on without first using the phone app.

Turns out both were my mistake (and somewhat the fault of the mediocre documentation/startup docs).

You can't access any scooter functions while its charging. So when you first open the box and logically go to charge it, double-tapping to turn on the headlights won't work. You may also need to adjust the screw at the base of the handlebar post. It used a different Allan key size than the included key, but tightening it up a bit will make it easier to open/close.

The app is sufficient. It definitely could use some user interface redesign - its lost opportunity to turn this into an exceptional product - but it suffices for what it is. I set the unit to hi regen on braking and "baby mode" for my first test runs.

Tires are hard. There is some give - but these feel pretty much like solid tires to me. If there is a honeycomb design inside, it will likely show itself on the most heinous road bumps and not by simply pushing a finger or pen into the tire material.

Shocks were pretty sticky when I tested them in my house. Not smooth at all. They loosened up considerably after a 5K test run. And about that test run...

I rode to a smooth track near my house and did about 10 laps. On the perfect surface I was able to focus on the acceleration and handling of the scooter. Very, very good. In S mode has a great pickup, and I achieved MAX speed in a few seconds. Braking was very good. I immediately came to a stop with double as well as single brakes. Regen seemed to bring me to a stop - but was not very aggressive feeling - even on max. That might be due to my weight.

I am a fit 215lbs and am 6' tall. Size 11 feet. The scooter feels like it was built for me. Deck is plenty spacious and handlebar grips are at the perfect height for me. I've been on scooters that felt fragile - this is NOT one of them. I pulled on the bars as I cornered and pushed on them as I braked. No wiggle. No squeek.

After the smooth track, I went to a nearby jacked-up parking lot, filled with cracks, weeds and bumps. The scooter handled 1" lips and 2-3" gaps in pavement well. The shocks did their jobs, but the wheels gave me little joy. I felt significant road vibration. Maybe the wheels need a break in period as well...

As for the weight and storage ... I commute using a folding bike (Dahon Vigor D9) and this scooter weighs significantly more (50%) and is much harder to handle when walking it or when folded. I've gotten into a habit of taking my Dahon with me everywhere possible and I fold it down quickly and roll it around or pick it up when I need to.

This is a bulky scooter and you won't want to pick it up and carry it often. I was able to use it as an unpowered kick scooter pretty easily. So running out of power when on the road should not be a problem. But multimodal commuting might be annoying if you have a lot of stairs to climb or will be on a tight train.

The charge outlet is well-protected with a spring loaded cap. There is also some rubber backing in the cap to help create a better water seal. Should be good for splashes. But I'd stay away from a puddle deep enough to immerse the bottom of the board.

The front and rear lights are very bright. No additional lights are needed.

Changes?

Improve the quality of the app. Make it so good/informative that people will want it open on the handlebar of the scooter while they're riding. Do more quality control of the text as well.

Maybe provide wheels with a tiny bit more cushion. Wheel tech is steadily improving and a softer core wheel (keep it solid) will definitely make folks happier. I can't imagine anyone wanting harder wheels.

Improve your documentation and startup tips card. Larger font. Clearer layout. Put things in order of importance for the best startup experience. A large, colorful startup tips card that says things like (lights won't turn on when charging, adjust handlebar base, etc). And change the screw on the handlebar base to the same size Allan key as the rest of the screws on the scooter. I have tools, some may not.

Excellent scooter and highly recommended!

----------------

Update:

Today I went for a 10 mile ride. I used ECO for 75% and SPORT mode for 25%. MAX speed almost all the way. There were three significant uphills (1/4 mile each) and several large downhills. I used regenerative braking as much as possible. When I got home I had 1 bar left, flashing.

I weight 215 lbs, which is approaching the upper limit of the scooter's spec. So on a full charge I can reliably get about 10 miles out of the scooter judiciously using SPORT mode. For me, this scooter is good since my office is 3 miles away from my house. I can just blast on SPORT both ways.

Since I've owned the scooter the APP has gone through an update adding a few new features. Its still pretty poor quality and does not seem to save my changes to settings like regenerative braking, etc.

------UPDATE-------

I've lowered the star rating by one due to the following issues.

1. Noise. The rear fender makes a LOT of noise when riding. Constant clunking sounds as it flops around. Its very irritating. They also break under the vibration load. I’M ON MY FOURTH REAR FENDER UNDER WARRANTY!!! AND IT JUST BROKE AS WELL. THEY ALL CRACK AND THEN BREAK AT THE SAME SPOT!!!

2. Range anxiety. From a full charge, the scooter drops down to one flashing bar at 8.5 miles on me, regularly. Far short of 25 miles and I'm wistful... It would make sense that the flashing bar is really 25% power remaining instead of 10% or less - but I don't want to test it. I usually need 10 miles of range when I ride the scooter (its a round trip) and I can just eek it out if I only use sport mode for the first 10-20% of my ride (when I need more speed to better negotiate car traffic). By the time I'm heading home using standard mode exclusively I'm stressing range. So I guess I can lose 15 lbs to get better range... Carrying the charger and recharging on the road is not an option in this use case.

3. Accelerator glitches. The scooter has gunned uncontrollably on two occasions. Both times I was sitting at a light, then I pressed the accelerator and the scooter took off at max speed and would not stop, even when I hit the brakes! I had to turn off the power... The first time I thought it was something I did. Second time I realized it was the scooter. VERY dangerous situations for me both times. I can only guess that it may have something to do with cruise control as it did not happen before I turned that on (may be coincidental). I'll turn off cruise control for the time being when riding in traffic/pedestrian settings and will try to replicate the issue in a parking lot and see if its some type of user error...

4. Aftermarket service has been excellent thus far. Yadea have sent me replacement parts for the rear fender. As well as PDF and video instructions on maintenance. Very responsive to requests. Scooter front shocks are still quite sticky. Can’t seem to lube or adjust them to be smoother. Side reflectors are a pain to get off in order to service rear wheel or replace rear fender. However, once you have performed maintenance on the scooter, repeat sessions are easy.
text_fidelity_b: YADEA Electric Scooter Adults, Foldable Commuting Electric Scooters KS5, 3 Adjustable Speeds Max 18.6 MPH, 25 Miles Long Range, Dual Shock Absorption, Front Suspension, Triple Brake, Cruise Control

text_fidelity_a: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black My husband and I bought this piece of equipment to add to our existing exercise equipment, and with the hope that it might boost my low bone density a bit.  I've been using it about 3 times a week for several months now, and while I don't think there is any weight loss (did not want it for that anyway), I definitely feel better after I've been on it for 10 minutes.  When I first started using it, I would stand with my feet about 14-15 inches apart, and an hour or so later would feel my back hurting a bit and I couldn't have the speed any higher than about 5 or 6.  So figured out that since this oscillates up and down from left to right (like a superfast see-saw), I would try standing with my feet much closer together.  The up and down movement would be greatly lessened so it wouldn't put so much pressure on the back after the 10 minute stand.  This worked beautifully and now as long as I keep my feet only about 4" apart I can turn the speed up much higher, it seems to eliminate residual stress in my system, and my back does not hurt at all after using it.  So how you place your feet and your posture also is very important in how you will feel after using this vibration plate.  I have yet to get my bone density rechecked so not sure if it has helped that or not, but I really like this machine a lot, am very glad we bought it and plan to keep using it for as long as it lasts.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent **Update** After a few uses, most everything is still wonderful. The zipper and the flap that protects it from the rain, are absolutely awful. Just about cut off the flap last camping outing. Otherwise--great!

Prior to getting this tent we borrowed a tent for a camping trip, and while we thought it set up quick and seemed nice, we were greeted by a deluge pouring through the seams on the roof. My wife was about ready to swear off camping, but we pushed on. We weren't going to let that happen again, so when I saw this tent, I pounced.

It comes in a rather large box, and the bag within is almost as large. It's large, vibrant, and has all the usual things you see in packaging (I imagine the bare bag is what you see in retail) on the sides. The real bonus was the expanding bottom of the bag, which makes it nice and neat for before the sale but expands to be a more realistic container after the first trip, where things don't tend to fit in their original bags.

That trip was eye opening. Not only is the sixty second assembly more or less legit (it kinda doubles when you include taking it out of the bag), it's an ample tent. I'm 6'7" and while I couldn't stand in in the tent, it's broad tall roof is such a blessing. Likewise the sides go up at a steep angle making all but the outer inches rather tall too. It's nice and airy and makes a very generous two person tent, though you could turn it into a flop house and squeeze 8 in. I'd say 4 is doable (without misery and with the little wall helping a bit), and 2 is luxurious, which is more than I'd say for most 8 person tents.

No leaks, quick setup, quick break down, and stylish looks are a big pluses.

Minuses are few and minor--mostly size of tent for storage (as the description notes, this isn't for backpacking). It's not the most compact, but really it's a slight difference and the quick setup is a great trade off and makes you want to actually use the tent!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent

text_fidelity_a:
YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity I bought one of these racks in June 2017 from REI, and have used it many times over the year. The rack is a good solution for my Mazda 5 roof bars, though it's somewhat challenging to get my fairly heavy Electra Townie on and off the car (I'm not a strong person).

I bought a second rack recently (December 2017). The new rack has a different "skewer" design than the old one. The old skewer had a "cap" on one end, and the locking/folding head screws on and off. The new skewer has the locking/folding head fixed to the bolt, and the cap on the opposite side screws on and off. My problem with the new design is that it's simply not as secure as the old one. With a lock core fitted and locked, the old locking head simply cannot be removed when a bike is clamped in (well, it could be by somebody with a hacksaw or something, but it's at least conceptually a sound system). Because the new skewer has a screw-off cap opposite the locking end, the lock is irrelevant: the screw can simply be removed and the bike is free.

The attached photo shows the old skewer ("A" and "B" for the locking head and the fixed end cap), and the new skewer ("C" for the locking head and "D" is the screw-off endcap).

Update: I heard back from Yakima support. Apparently there's a mechanism in the new endcap on the skewer that does pretty much what the spring-loaded sleeve on the old locking mechanism did. When the cap is tight against the fork, it actually cannot be removed at all easily. So two stars back :)
text_fidelity_b: YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer As there are plenty of reviews, I'm going to do a review that assumes you've read the rest and I will try and hit some of the criticisms. I've owned my DMT for about a month and a half. I'm not an overly picky or difficult person, as some reviewers seem to be. Not criticizing them, just letting you know that I may be easier going than you are. I got mine at $2399 so for me this was a bit of an investment and I read all the reviews I could find. Since Smooth only seems to publish the great reviews on their website, I am publishing mine here. I do think the Treadmill Doctor reviews are fair and accurate, but they seem to have a chummy relationship with Smooth.

I ordered the unit and the Smooth Sync Bluetooth module. I ordered it with the white glove service as I'm lazy and it's heavy. First, the ordering process, here is my timeline:

- 12 Jan 13, Order placed with Smooth via web
- 12 Jan 13, Email confirmation of order
- 18 Jan 13, Credit card charged
- 18 Jan 13 Product Shipped Notice
- 27 Jan 13, Contacted by shipping/assembly company
- 28 Jan 13, Product received/assembled
- 29 Jan 13, Smooth Sync received/installed

The unit arrived in one large box and one ridiculously large box. It would have been difficult for my 21 year-old son and I to get it in the house. Unless you are awfully burly or have moving equipment (a standard dolly won't get it) then at least have it delivered to the room where you want to set it up. When assembled, even using the wheels, if I moved it by myself I would be hurting the next day. As others have said, the assembly duo (from CEVA Logistics) had never seen one before, but had assembled similar items. They assembled it correctly without damage to the unit or anything else in about an hour. I'm pretty handy and I think I could have done it a bit quicker. If you assemble it yourself, you are primarily assembling the upright portion. When we tried using it the first time, something was banging. They disassembled one section, reassembled and everything was grand.

Smooth forgot to ship the Smooth Sync so it wasn't available day one, but UPS ground got it here the next day. It installed in just a few minutes with no problems.

I did quite a bit of research before buying. I use ellipticals at the gym and I own a top of the line Bowflex. The Agile DMT replaced a Proform 7.0 Treadmill that gave up the ghost after 14 years and several moves. In terms of engineering, construction and features, there is absolutely no comparison between this and my Proform. This is a gym quality machine with more features than any gym will ever pay for. Contrary to what others have said, the speakers are not bad. The fan is a bit cheap, but on the highest setting it provides a little breeze. The display/control panel is functional but not impressive.

Others commented on all the plastic. While it seems a little silly, it does cover a lot of the moving parts such that you can move around the device without hooking or snagging and it prevents dust and dirt and will make it easier to clean.

As I mentioned, I bought the Smooth Sync. While $130 seems like a lot, if you consider that you are paying for the hardware, the app and the integration, it is not bad. The MySmooth app is good. The video application is interesting, but definitely not something I would pay $20 a video for. It appears Smooth spent quite a lot to shoot the videos. In the current market, they would probably be better off letting users upload their own with the MySmooth app controlling the speed of play. The Android app does not record workouts and accessing the History button crashes the application. Smooth does not have a page with news about the app.

As for customer service, I've never received any response from Smooth that appeared remotely human. It took 6 days to get another email after I placed my order. When the CEVA tracking showed that my machine had been in town for a week and I had received no call, I sent an email to Smooth. I got no reply, but I noted on the bill of lading that Smooth had contacted CEVA and told them to get moving. CEVA called me the day after I sent the email (email Saturday, call Sunday, delivery Monday). When I sent Smooth an email to ask about my Smooth Sync (several weeks after I ordered it) my response was the UPS email notice with no other response. The device arrived the next day via UPS ground. In my book, this is adequate but certainly well below average. I would have expected the order confirmation to provide some type of information on when I could expect a follow-up on shipping. I would have expected them to ship my Smooth Sync so that it was here when the machine arrived. For the price, I would expect at least a follow-up email to see how the delivery/install went and if I had any problems. All of this would really merit a "very good" not an "exceptional" these days. I get follow-up emails from eBay sellers to see if I'm satisfied with a .99 cable.

Smooth was recently purchased. The new owner is continuing the product line and honoring all warranties, etc. Supposedly they are investing millions. Hopefully the person in charge of customer service takes his or her buyout and moves on to be replaced by someone more competent. I say that as I think the products are excellent, so it is too bad when one person brings the company down to simply being good.

As for the white glove delivery install, I live in the DC area. If you don't get experienced assembly people here, odds are you won't elsewhere. My installers got it together with no problems and didn't take all day. I'm satisfied and would do it again.
text_fidelity_b: Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Kool Stop D. Ace Bicycle Brake Pads These things absolutely rock! I've used Swiss Stop pads, which are fantastic, but are no better than Kool Stop and are significantly more expensive. I can only speak for the black/salmon dual brake pads, but as a Seattle commuter I can say that they are amazing on my hilly, wet commute. The feel of the pads is great--nice gentle engagement without grabbing, and progressive feel throughout the stroke.

This is one of those cheap and easy (seriously, two allen keys and 10 minutes) upgrades that will have you wondering why you waited so long on your stock pads. If you're one of those people who feel the need to spend money on their bike to feel faster, or you can't imagine having an American component on your Italian thoroughbred, go ahead and get the SwissStop brake pads. If you don't, however, have a fetish for ever more expensive bike components go ahead and get the Kool Stop pads and with the money you save get yourself a nice espresso and a croissant on your next few rides.
text_fidelity_b: Kool Stop D. Ace Bicycle Brake Pads

text_fidelity_a: Teeter EZ-Up Gravity Boots I AM BATMAN! These Teeter Hang Ups are just what I needed to help with my back pain. I do a lot of dead lifts and squats so my spine is constantly taking a compacting toll. These are comfortable to use once you find the sweet spot on your shins to fix them to. I think that they look goofy so I don't take them to the gym but pair them with a pull up bar at home instead. WARNING: I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND USING THIS PRODUCT ALONE. If you are to fatigued to pull yourself up then that could lead to a very bad situation. Remember to either have someone there or affix some rope or something to your bar to help you pull yourself back up if you are too tired to do so. Over all great quality and you can literally feel your spine decompressing as you hang there. You can also do crunches and reverse squats while hanging. I do it for about 3 minutes a day twice a day but I should do it more as it is so relieving. I swear I am getting taller too!
text_fidelity_b: Teeter EZ-Up Gravity Boots

text_fidelity_a:
Weslo Cadence R 5.2 Treadmill I've had this for a little while now. I'm short and overweight, and usually fail at my daily walking goals, BUT, I've been very pleased with this purchase. Being the aforementioned short and overweight, the preset workouts are just a bit much for me, but it wouldn't take too much work to get there, I don't think. Probably my favorite feature is its simplicity. A lot of people want bells and whistles and wouldn't be happy with this, but it's perfect for this not-athletic person. I'll never get up to the faster speeds, but to be honest, it shakes enough under my weight when I attempt a light jog, that I'd be just a little leery of pushing it any more. Otherwise it feels sturdy though, and I'm not afraid of it breaking or anything.

As others have said, a second set of hands really helps when putting it together initially. It's not hard, just awkward. My mom helped me by just holding things still or handing me parts. It maybe took a half hour from start to finish, and I was taking my time. Getting it exactly where I wanted in my small room was the hardest part. Folding it up is easy - it's heavy, but I'd be scared to use anything lighter!

This is my first treadmill, and I think it's perfect for a casual user. I doubt I'll ever be an avid walker/jogger, but this at least gives me ample opportunities for exercise when I need it, without worrying about time of day or weather.
text_fidelity_b: Weslo Cadence R 5.2 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall I was an Eagle Scout and we've used these bags a few times in temps down to freezing, and they work great if you get a fleece bag liner and put it in there. We were really nice and toasty warm.

PROS:
- HUGE - really really big. I'm 6ft and not small, and there's loads of extra room. If you don't like being cramped, look no further.
- WARM - It's actually pretty darn warm on it's own.
- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.
https://www.amazon.com/Stansport-Fleece-Sleeping-Bag-Red/dp/B002YXITMW/ref=sr_1_7?dchild=1&keywords=fleece+sleeping+bag+liner&qid=1592870476&sr=8-7

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall

text_fidelity_a: SCHWALBE Marathon Supreme HS 382 Touring Road Bike Tire (700x35, Triple Nano Folding, Reflex) In my case, that answer is yes.  The Schwalbe Marathon Supreme (700x38) is the prefect tire for my bike and the style of riding I do. I've used other tires, most recently a Continental gator skin (700x35)  that I put over 3000 miles on with no problems, flats or complaints. They were, and are, great tires for me. When I was getting ready to replace the Conti's I decided to throw on the old Schwalbe Marathon Supremes that came stock on the bike (700x40) that probably had well over 3000 miles on them and could not believe how much smoother these old, worn out Schwalbe's felt when compared to the old, worn out Contis's. Again- no knock on the Conti's. Just seat of the pants observation. The 700x40 were a little bigger than I wanted so I went down to a 700x38 as I never liked the way the 700x40 fit under my fenders. The 700x38 are perfection on my bike for my style of riding. It is like riding on a sure footed cloud. They roll so beautifully. I appreciate the added visibility of the reflective side wall. It is everything you expect and I feel like the manufacturer has gone above and beyond when it comes to the hardware on this jump rope.

First, the handles are my favorite. They have an internal metal ball that swivels effortlessly through a sturdy plastic collar. This set up creates the most effortless jump rope turning you have ever encountered. All you need to do is flip the rope in the direction you want it to go and the ball bearings seem to do the rest with the smallest flicks of your wrists.

The cable is exactly that - sturdy wire CABLE - with a protective plastic coating. It whips through the air and it doesn't hurt that much at all if it strikes you when you misstep (and that is coming from someone who bruises easily). The cable can kink if you fold it and pinch it really hard, which is probably why the seller includes a second cable so you don't have to order a whole new jump rope nor jump with a wonky, crinkled cable. I thought that was a very thoughtful touch.

The hardware that makes the jump rope adjustable is really neat and unlike anything else I have seen. It's actually a tiny screw-bolt on each end of the rope that tightens down onto the cable giving you a no slip sizing option. Again, this is a very thoughtful touch, both for those who are tall and short. (The jump rope worked just fine for my 5'10" hubby and 5'7" me.)

The green color is not quite the electric neon color shown but is more a pleasant grass green. I uploaded a picture taken in natural light so you can get a good idea of what the color is like in real life. It's a great unisex color that is not too girlie and is easy to spot in your gym bag or the stash of work out at home gear. It was easy to roll up after using and slides effortlessly back into it's nylon storage pouch.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this product at a discount to try it out and write a review. This jump rope is not junk, this is a quality fitness item that has had some impressive thought and effort put into its design. Rest assured you are buying a good, quality item!

text_fidelity_a:
Tents for Camping- Instant Tent, 2/4 People, Ultralight Easy Quick Set Up Tent, Double-Layer Waterproof Camping Tent, Perfect House Shelters for Hiking, Camping, Hunting, Fishing, Outdoor… First, we are not tent experts. While my wife and I have slept in tents as kids, as adults we have no experience. We decided to try this tent; 1. for use at the beach, 2. because we have been invited to tent camp and MIGHT try it, 3. it comes apart into 2 pieces and allows for different uses.

We had never even considered it until we saw this pop up kind. We had no interest in trying to figure out how to put a tent together. But this one... turns out it works great! We decide to take it out this last weekend - of course it was hugely windy - but we gave it a try. While yes, the wind made it an adventure, it still worked well. As we followed the steps we pulled out the tent, opened it, and the pop up portion went into place. We didn’t figure out right away there was a “lock” position - the picture above shows it BEFORE we popped it into that lock position and during the wind so it is blowing a bit - but even before the pop, it was “fully,” but once it was popped, it was perfect. Taking it out of the locked position was easy and quick. It took 2 tries to get the thing down correctly and folded - step by step with the instructions finally worked. But the instructions were done so we could finally figure it out. The tent has a ground cloth for under - it says if you’re just doing the outer part, but I think we’d use it for both the tent and outer cover. There are two parts to the tent - the enclosed tent and the outer top shell - you can use them together or separately. The sides have venting windows, and there are both front and back “doors” that have both a screen and solid cover. The materials seem good to us - however we both feel like we’ve seen/felt thicker or at least a different material on other tents, so we do wonder the longevity and quality while feeling like this is a good tent. Again, we are not experts, but for taking to the beach, we feel like we’ll have a nice tent and cover to make for a nice day. We’re not sure we will tent camp, but the next time we’re asked, we’ll be ready to maybe give it a try for a night. This seems like a good tent and we are glad we grabbed it.
text_fidelity_b: Tents for Camping- Instant Tent, 2/4 People, Ultralight Easy Quick Set Up Tent, Double-Layer Waterproof Camping Tent, Perfect House Shelters for Hiking, Camping, Hunting, Fishing, Outdoor…

text_fidelity_a:
Tommaso Avventura - Holiday Special Pricing - Shimano Sora Gravel Adventure Bike with Disc Brakes, Extra Wide Tires, and Carbon Fork, Road Or Dirt Trail Touring, Matte Black Usage : Everyday commute, weekend long trips.

This is my first bike after about 10 years. Overall I am pleased with the bike.

Cons:
- It runs on the heavier side and you can feel the weight, but I could not find anything much lighter in similar dollar range. Again it's not too heavy. I carried the bike after an accident for about 2 miles.
- Carrying the bike isn't the easiest. I wish the ergonomics allowed for that better.
- Seat could be a little softer but it's not the bike's fault. You can easily find a better seat. I have used the seat for longer rides and it gets painful after about 2 hours for me. So not bad at all.

Pros:
- The brakes are really good. They can bring you to a halt in a pretty high grade descent really fast if you need that to happen. Of course they need tuning and maintenance like anything else.
- The handlebars are very comfortable. I loved the overall handling of the bike.
- Riding it is fun. I went for a 5 hour ride. The bike maintained it's fun except the hard seat.
- Giantnerd's ready to ride made it possible to get this bike rolling out in 20 mins. Highly recommended.

Overall, I would highly recommend this bike to someone who is new, is on budget or needs a bike for daily commute and occasional long rides. So basically everyone except pros could use this bike.
text_fidelity_b: Tommaso Avventura - Holiday Special Pricing - Shimano Sora Gravel Adventure Bike with Disc Brakes, Extra Wide Tires, and Carbon Fork, Road Or Dirt Trail Touring, Matte Black
